correctness.rationale: For the four ones the counts of preceding zeros are a, a+b, N-a-b, N-a. Reversal gives D_100=D_001=H and D_110=D_011; D_011=6a+3b+c=N+t for t=4a+b, and the count of 101 is 6b+4c=4N-2t. Each one contributes z_i(N-z_i) to 010, giving 2N(N-1)-2H. The 000 and 111 counts are fixed, including N<3. Summing binom(z_i,2) gives the stated quadratic in a at fixed N,t, so the only possible distinct partner is its reflected root, a'=a+(b-c)/5. Then b'=b-4(b-c)/5 and c'=c+6(b-c)/5. Orient by b>c, since b'-c'=-(b-c); the divisibility condition gives d>=1 and all partner gaps are then nonnegative. This proves all in-class fibers, including empty gaps. The unique parametrization gives N=2a+3c+10d and the generating series, the distinct-deck count, and the exact attainable lengths (subtract 10 and use the semigroup of 2 and 3). For fixed d the count from 2a+3c=N-10d is (N-10d)/6+O(1); summation gives N^2/120+O(N) compared to N^2/8+O(N) words, hence 2/15. Independently enumerating triples of positions in the length-14 pair gives (120,65,50,15,65,30,15,4) in both cases. The exact replay is the algebra in RESULT.md lines 31–69; verify.py and verify_output.txt were inspected as bounded corroboration. No unrestricted fiber-size claim follows.

evidence: Using S_1 fixes t, so b=t-4a, c=N+6a-2t. The remaining equality in S_2 reduces directly to (a-a')(10(a+a')+2N-6t)=0. Its distinct root shifts a by (b-c)/5. Integrality is equivalent to b-c being a multiple of 5; choosing b>c makes nonnegativity automatic for both words.

The resulting free parameters a,c>=0, d>=1 obey N=2a+3c+10d. Multiplying their three geometric series and taking the leading count give the claimed series and 2/15 with no extra deck-combinatorial argument.

Under the exact-invariant value standard, however, the known complete moment criterion and routine one-dimensional elimination already determine the purported new classification and census.
